tyler (Docs): Heads-up: the /v1/rerank reference shows "score" as a 0-1 normalized value in the example, but our API currently returns raw logits. Customers are parsing it as probability and getting weird results.

hao (API): You're right. We returned logits for flexibility. We didn't update the example after the SDK added a normalization helper. Backend will keep logits. Docs should show raw logits and an example of how to convert to probabilities.

rina (SDK): I can update the JS/Python snippets to show `from math import exp` normalization example and call out the SDK helper `client.rerank.normalize_scores(resp)`. That should prevent breaks.

tyler (Docs): Can you paste a minimal mapping snippet I can drop into the page? One line curl + one-line Python normalization comment would be ideal.

rina (SDK): Curl minimal: ```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
 -d '{"model":"rank-1","query":"q","candidates":["a","b"]}'
```
Python normalization example (inline): `probs = [math.exp(s)/sum(math.exp(x) for x in scores) for s in scores]  # convert logits -> normalized probs`
Also add note: `SDK provides client.rerank.normalize_scores(resp)` for convenience.

hao (API): That sounds good. I'll add a short sentence in the API contract section clarifying that "score" is a raw logit.

tyler (Docs): Draft blurb: "Note: the API returns raw logits in `score`. Convert to probabilities client-side (see snippet) or use the SDK helper `client.rerank.normalize_scores`." I'll include the curl + python one-liner and a tiny JSON Schema showing `score` as number.
